review_stage: Independent post-round confirmation; original quality-row report preserved
finding: Golden audit-history SQL LIMIT 5000 and loss of an older OFFER_APPROVED audit-feed row
assessment: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED: capped audit-feed loss is established; failure of the public readable-history requirement is not established
confirmed_observation: The indexed API probe observes a successful ordinary offer approval and its audit row id 6, then performs 5,050 successful logins. The offer remains COMMITTED, the normal bootstrap audit array has 5,000 entries, and id 6 is absent. The frozen source explains this directly: src/index.js:102 appends one LOGIN audit row on each login; :222 selects audit_log ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5000. The normal Audit log table is constructed only from boot.audit (public/js/hireops.js:322,397-411). There is no pagination control or GET audit-row/history endpoint exposing the omitted raw audit_log entry. Reload and fresh sign-in refresh bootstrap (public/js/app.js:264-270,290-305), so they do not recover that capped table row.
normal_ui_alternative: The same normal Audit Trail page also renders the uncapped after_images collection. src/index.js:215-216 selects every after-image; receipt():278-284 writes both the structured before/after snapshot and the readable audit line for each successful action. The approval transaction invokes that function at :346. Login only appends an audit_log row and does not erase or replace after_images. public/js/hireops.js:381-394 renders each after-image as an ordinary expandable receipt card, with APPROVE plus offer id, actor and timestamp in the summary and labeled Before/After sections with readable field values in the body. Lines 412-415 render all such cards on the Audit Trail screen. Therefore the HISTORY-OFFER approval and its immutable before/after facts remain normally accessible through its receipt card, even when the separate audit-log table loses its raw prose row. This alternative is established by source tracing, not a new browser observation.
public_requirement_assessment: Frozen hireops_rules.md:373-384 requires an append-only human-readable audit record and a structured after-image, persistence of both, and readable receipts in the Audit Trail. Section 9 at :405-407 asks for every action to remain a readable line with a before/after summary after reload or fresh sign-in. The probe demonstrates truncation of one presentation/feed, not deletion of either stored history record or loss of the action and before/after history from the Audit Trail. The receipt card supplies the readable event identity and expandable before/after summary through ordinary controls. The public rules do not require a particular table, the literal OFFER_APPROVED token, or the exact generated audit.detail sentence to remain the only acceptable representation. I therefore do not independently confirm this as a public-contract failure solely from the supplied probe. Calling this loss of audit history, missing receipt, or absent normal UI access would overstate the finding. A narrower statement that the separate raw audit-log feed silently omits older entries is supported.
removing_limit_assessment: Removing the hard LIMIT 5000 from the task-specific solution bootstrap query is a reasonable small robustness improvement: it would keep the existing Audit log table complete without changing rules, shared harness policy, authorization, or receipt semantics. It is not required by a confirmed history-loss defect on the current evidence, because the normal after-image cards retain an acceptable readable history. For a larger product, accessible pagination could preserve the same completeness without returning every row; neither layout is mandated. If the coordinator elects to change this query, bind the changed source to a new candidate and check the resulting normal UI rather than presenting this report as a runtime validation of the proposed edit.
